actions.subject_label: Mirae Asset ELSS Tax Saver - Direct Growth
actions.headline: Mirae Asset ELSS Tax Saver - Direct Growth and UTI Nifty 50 Index Fund - Direct Growth overlap 100% -- you are paying twice for one exposure
reasons: The two funds share 100% of their disclosed holdings (51% of total fund value, since factsheets publish only the largest positions).
Largest shared names: HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, RELIANCE, INFY.
Holding both adds cost and admin without adding diversification.

2 further fund pair(s) overlap above 55%: Axis Bluechip Fund - Regular Growth / Mirae Asset ELSS Tax Saver - Direct Growth at 99%; Axis Bluechip Fund - Regular Growth / UTI Nifty 50 Index Fund - Direct Growth at 99%
actions.portfolio_impact: Consolidating simplifies the portfolio without changing exposure
actions.tax_impact: Switching between funds is a redemption for tax; check the gain on the smaller holding before acting
risks: Consolidating into one fund concentrates manager risk
counterarguments: Two funds with the same holdings can still behave differently in a drawdown if their cash and turnover policies differ
Overlap is measured from published holdings, which lag by a month
alternatives: Stop contributions to Mirae Asset ELSS Tax Saver - Direct Growth and let it run down rather than selling
Keep both but redirect new money to a genuinely different strategy

actions.headline: Debt is -5.6% outside its band -- point contributions here rather than selling elsewhere
reasons: Debt is at 17.4% against a target of 30.0% (band 23%-37%).

Redirecting contributions closes the gap in about 7 months without selling anything or triggering tax.

actions.tax_impact: None: redirection uses future contributions, so nothing is realised

counterarguments: If the drift came from a deliberate view you still hold, the policy band is the thing to change, not the portfolio
alternatives: Redirect contributions instead of selling
Widen the band in the IPS if this drift is acceptable to you
